formation.title: The Reunification of the Maya
formation.text:
For generations, the Maya world has been a mosaic of rival city-states, the legacy of Mayapan's collapse, the wars between the K'iche' and Kaqchikel, the ambitions of a dozen petty lords. Now, through conquest and diplomacy, the scattered Maya polities have been drawn together under a single authority. The sacbe roads connect our cities, the observatories track the stars, and the codex-keepers record our laws. But what vision shall guide this reunited Maya realm? Shall we be remembered as the inheritors of our ancestors' celestial wisdom, a civilization whose calendar, writing, and astronomical knowledge made them the scholars of the Americas? Or shall we forge a military confederation in the tradition of the great Halach Uinic, binding our warriors into an army that can defend the Maya heartland against any who would challenge us?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We are the keepers of time and knowledge.

modifiers.name: Lords of the Calendar
modifiers.text: The Maya are the keepers of time itself. Through generations of astronomical observation and mathematical precision, our daykeepers have mapped the movements of Venus, predicted eclipses, and woven the sacred calendar into every aspect of governance and daily life. This mastery of celestial knowledge guides our people forward.

options.text: The True Men shall rule as one.

modifiers.name: Confederation of the Halach Uinic
modifiers.text: The true lords of the Maya lands have spoken with one voice. Under the authority of the Halach Uinic, the True Man, the scattered city-states have been bound together into a confederation of shared purpose. Our Holcan warriors stand ready, our Nacom war leaders have been chosen, and the white roads carry the march of unified armies.

advances.name: Holcan Warriors
advances.text: The Holcan are the professional warrior caste of the Maya, full-time soldiers trained from youth, armed with obsidian weapons and protected by cotton armor.

event.title: The Call of the Holcan
event.text: The Holcan, the professional warrior caste of the Maya, trace their traditions back centuries. Unlike the conscripted farmers who fight in most armies, the Holcan are full-time soldiers: trained from youth in the arts of war, organized under the command of elected Nacom war leaders, and honored with status that places them among the elite of Maya society. Their cotton-quilted armor, the ichcahuipilli, has proven effective against both obsidian blades and European musket balls at close range. Their jungle warfare tactics, ambushes in dense forest, coordinated night raids, the devastating use of the atlatl spear-thrower, have frustrated invaders for generations. With the formation of the Maya state, the Holcan tradition has been formally enshrined as the backbone of our military.

options.text: The Holcan shall defend our people.

advances.name: Sacbe Trade Roads
advances.text: The sacbe, raised limestone causeways, connect Maya cities across the jungle, enabling trade caravans to travel even during the rainy season.

advances.name: Milpa Agriculture
advances.text: The milpa system of intercropping maize, beans, and squash sustains dense Maya populations in the tropical lowlands.

advances.name: Hieroglyphic Writing
advances.text: Maya hieroglyphic script, the only fully developed writing system of pre-Columbian Americas, records history, astronomy, and law on stone monuments and bark-paper codices.

advances.name: Astronomical Tradition
advances.text: Maya astronomers track the cycles of Venus, predict eclipses, and calibrate the sacred calendar with remarkable precision from dedicated stone observatories.

advances.name: Halach Uinic Governance
advances.text: The Halach Uinic, True Man, governs the Maya polity with the counsel of the Ah Cuch Cab nobility, balancing the authority of the city-state lords.

advances.name: Ichcahuipilli Craft
advances.text: Maya armorers produce the ichcahuipilli, quilted cotton body armor soaked in brine, which provides effective protection against obsidian weapons and even early firearms.

advances.name: Obsidian Mastery
advances.text: Maya weaponsmiths achieve mastery in knapping obsidian into razor-sharp blades for the macuahuitl, a devastating sword embedded with volcanic glass teeth.

advances.name: Mayapan League
advances.text: The League of Mayapan unified the great families of Yucatan under a shared council, providing collective governance over trade, defense, and law.

event.title: The Refounding of the League
event.text: The League of Mayapan once united the great families of Yucatan under a shared council, the Cocom, the Xiu, the Chel, and others sitting together to adjudicate disputes, coordinate trade, and plan defense against outsiders. When Mayapan fell to internal treachery around 1448, the League shattered into sixteen rival provinces, and a century of fratricidal warfare followed. Now that the Maya cities are reunited, the question arises: shall we restore the League's centralized authority, with a single ruling house directing the affairs of all provinces? Or shall we embrace a looser federation, where each province retains its autonomy under a shared council of equals?

options.text: One house shall lead all others.

modifiers.name: Restored Authority
modifiers.text: The centralized authority of a single ruling house brings order and stability to the Maya provinces.

options.text: The council of equals shall endure.

modifiers.name: Council of Equals
modifiers.text: A federation of autonomous provinces, united by shared council, preserves the diversity and loyalty of the Maya peoples.

advances.name: Maritime War Canoes
advances.text: The great dugout canoes of the Maya, capable of carrying forty men and vast quantities of trade goods, dominate the coastal waters from Xicalango to Honduras.

advances.name: Popol Vuh
advances.text: The sacred Book of the Community preserves the K'iche' creation narrative, the exploits of the Hero Twins, and the genealogy of Maya lords.

event.title: The Legacy of the Popol Vuh
event.text: The Popol Vuh, the Book of the Community, has been preserved and taught to a new generation. This sacred narrative of the K'iche' Maya tells of the creation of the world, the exploits of the Hero Twins Hunahpu and Xbalanque in the underworld of Xibalba, and the origin of the K'iche' people from white and yellow corn. More than a story, it is the foundation of Maya cosmology, morality, and identity. The daykeepers who guard this wisdom now ask how it should shape our nation. Shall the Popol Vuh serve as a wellspring of learning, its astronomical observations, agricultural wisdom, and philosophical insights driving our scholars forward? Or shall it serve as a unifying creed, its creation myth and heroic tales binding our diverse peoples into one identity?

options.text: Let its wisdom illuminate our scholars.

modifiers.name: Wisdom of the Hero Twins
modifiers.text: The astronomical and philosophical insights of the Popol Vuh guide our scholars toward deeper understanding.

options.text: Let its stories bind our people as one.

modifiers.name: Children of the Corn
modifiers.text: The creation story of the K'iche', that humanity was fashioned from white and yellow corn, binds our diverse peoples in shared identity.

advances.name: Cacao Economy
advances.text: Cacao beans serve simultaneously as currency, ritual offering, and luxury commodity, the foundation of Maya commercial life.

event.title: The Cacao Lords
event.text: Cacao is more than a crop to the Maya: it is currency, ritual offering, diplomatic gift, and the drink of kings. The great cacao plantations of Tabasco and the Soconusco coast have made their lords fabulously wealthy, and cacao beans circulate as money throughout Mesoamerica. The maritime traders of the Yucatan coast carry cacao in their great canoes from Xicalango to Honduras and beyond. Now our reunified realm must decide how to harness this cacao wealth. Shall we prioritize the export trade, sending our cacao to foreign markets and drawing their goods to our shores? Or shall we formalize cacao beans as the official currency of the realm, stabilizing our economy through this universally valued commodity?

options.text: Let our canoes carry cacao to the world.

modifiers.name: Cacao Trade Routes
modifiers.text: Our maritime and overland traders carry cacao to markets across Mesoamerica and beyond.

options.text: Cacao shall be the currency of the realm.

modifiers.name: The Bean Standard
modifiers.text: Cacao beans serve as the universal medium of exchange, stabilizing commerce across our realm.

advances.name: Pyramid Architecture
advances.text: The great stepped pyramids of the Maya serve as temples, astronomical observatories, and symbols of divine authority aligned with celestial events.

advances.name: Nacom Command
advances.text: The Nacom, elected war leaders serving three-year terms, direct Maya military campaigns and preside over the annual martial rites in the month of Pax.

advances.name: K'iche' Expansion
advances.text: The aggressive K'iche' state conquered much of the Guatemalan highlands through rapid military campaigns, creating a model of Maya imperial warfare.

advances.name: Atlatl Warfare
advances.text: The atlatl spear-thrower allows Maya skirmishers to hurl darts with devastating force and accuracy from concealment in the dense jungle.

advances.name: Codex Tradition
advances.text: Maya scribes record astronomical tables, religious rituals, and historical chronicles on bark-paper codices folded like accordion screens.

advances.name: Highland Diplomacy
advances.text: The complex web of alliances, marriages, and rivalries between Maya highland kingdoms, K'iche', Kaqchikel, Tz'utujil, Mam, has refined the art of Maya statecraft.

advances.name: Coastal Trade Ports
advances.text: Ports like Tulum, Xicalango, and Naco serve as entrepots where maritime and overland trade routes converge, channeling obsidian, jade, salt, and cacao.

advances.name: Fortified Acropolis
advances.text: Maya cities build fortified acropolises, elevated citadels with defensive walls and towers, to protect their ruling families and temple complexes.

advances.name: Holcan Veteran Tradition
advances.text: The most experienced Holcan warriors form an elite cadre, their battlefield knowledge passed down through rigorous training in jungle combat and siege defense.

advances.name: Jungle Resistance
advances.text: The dense jungles of the Maya heartland become a weapon against invaders, disease, heat, and ambush consume armies that dare enter without invitation.

advances.name: Batab Administration
advances.text: The Batab, local governors appointed by the Halach Uinic, administer justice, collect tribute, and maintain order in each Maya province.

advances.name: Salt Trade Expansion
advances.text: The salt beds of the northern Yucatan coast produce a commodity essential to every Mesoamerican kitchen, making salt traders among the wealthiest in the Maya world.

advances.name: Defensive Confederacy
advances.text: Faced with external threats, the Maya city-states formalize mutual defense pacts, pooling their levies under shared command when any member is attacked.

advances.name: Calendar Keepers
advances.text: The daykeepers maintain the sacred 260-day Tzolk'in and 365-day Haab calendars, synchronizing them into the 52-year Calendar Round that governs ritual and political life.

advances.name: Itza Independence
advances.text: The Itza Maya at Tayasal on Lake Peten Itza maintained their independence until 1697, the last unconquered Maya state, a testament to the resilience of Maya civilization.

advances.name: Lacustrine Warfare
advances.text: The Maya of the Peten lakes master warfare on water, using canoe fleets to control the lakeshores and deny invaders the use of waterways.

advances.name: Tribute System
advances.text: Subject communities deliver cacao, cotton, jade, feathers, and labor to the ruling city, sustaining the Maya elite and funding public works.

advances.name: Forest Fortifications
advances.text: Palisades, ditches, and concealed defensive works blend into the forest landscape, creating layered fortifications that exploit the jungle terrain.

advances.name: Ch'orti' Military
advances.text: The Ch'orti' Maya of the southeastern highlands maintain a fierce military tradition, their warriors renowned for disciplined infantry tactics and mountain warfare.

advances.name: Syncretic Adaptation
advances.text: Pragmatic Maya leaders integrate foreign ideas and practices into their own traditions, preserving core identity while adapting to a changing world.

advances.name: Cultural Endurance
advances.text: Despite centuries of external pressure, Maya language, calendar, weaving traditions, and community governance endure as living practice rather than mere memory.

advances.name: Modern Confederation
advances.text: The Maya polity embraces modern governance structures while retaining the council-based decision-making that has served the Maya for millennia.

advances.name: Agricultural Renewal
advances.text: New agricultural techniques supplement the ancient milpa system, increasing yields while preserving the intercropping wisdom of Maya farmers.

advances.name: Maya National Identity
advances.text: A sense of shared Maya identity transcends the old city-state rivalries, uniting diverse linguistic communities under a common civilizational heritage.

advances.name: Reforged Army
advances.text: The Maya military adopts modern tactics and training methods while preserving the jungle warfare traditions that have defined Maya combat for centuries.

advances.name: Trade Revival
advances.text: The ancient trade networks of the Maya, once carrying obsidian, jade, and cacao along sacbe roads and coastal canoe routes, are restored and expanded.

destiny.name: Destiny of the Maya
destiny.text: The Maya have been reunited under a single banner. Now the question is what direction this reborn civilization will take: will it pursue the path of celestial knowledge or military confederation?

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Destiny of the Reunited Maya
event.text: For the first time in centuries, the Maya world speaks with one voice. The fractured city-states, the warring provinces of Yucatan, the highland kingdoms of Guatemala, all have been drawn together under a single authority. The sacbe roads carry traders and ambassadors between cities that once faced each other across barricades. The question now is not whether the Maya can endure, but what they will become.

options.text: A new era dawns for the Maya.

destiny.name: Calendar Wisdom
destiny.text: Seize the astronomical centers of Mesoamerica. By controlling Cholula's great temple and the pyramids of Teotihuacan, the Maya calendar-keepers will absorb the knowledge of all civilizations.

conditions.text: Chose Lords of the Calendar
Own Cholollan, or a subject owns it
Own Teōtīhuacān, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 1000

event.title: The Libraries of the Conquered
event.text: Our calendar-keepers have entered the great temples of the Valley of Mexico: Cholula's towering pyramid, the ancient observatories of Teotihuacan. Where other conquerors would have burned these places, our scholars reverently catalogued their astronomical records, their mathematical systems, their histories. The Maya tradition of knowledge has always been syncretic, absorbing and refining the learning of others. Now the accumulated wisdom of all Mesoamerica flows into our scribal schools.

options.text: Their knowledge enriches our own.

destiny.name: Venus Tables
destiny.text: Maya astronomers have refined the Venus Tables to unprecedented accuracy, predicting the movements of the morning star centuries in advance. Chichen Itza, where the round tower of the Caracol is sighted on the extremes of Venus, is built up as the city of the observers, and observatories are raised in two cities to keep the watch. This knowledge drives agricultural planning, trade cycles, and statecraft.

conditions.text: A Maya Observatory stands in at least 2 of our locations
We own Chichen Itza and its development is at least 11
Prestige at least 50

event.title: The Refinement of the Venus Tables
event.text: Our astronomers have achieved something remarkable. By cross-referencing the ancient records of Teotihuacan with our own centuries of Venus observations, they have refined the Dresden Codex tables to predict the rising and setting of the morning star with a margin of error of less than two hours over five centuries. This is not merely an academic achievement: the Venus cycle governs our agricultural calendar, our trade schedules, and the timing of war and peace. Shall we direct this knowledge toward scholarly advancement and infrastructure, or toward expanding our trade networks?

options.text: Let our scholars build upon this foundation.

modifiers.name: Scholars of the Morning Star
modifiers.text: Maya astronomers apply Venus cycle predictions to long-range planning of trade and intelligence gathering, though the scholarly focus diverts resources from military upkeep.

options.text: Let our merchants profit from this knowledge.

modifiers.name: Merchants of the Morning Star
modifiers.text: Maya traders time their voyages to the Venus cycle, securing favorable credit and faster ship construction while their communities recover swiftly from setbacks.

destiny.name: The New B'ak'tun
destiny.text: A new great cycle of the Long Count has dawned. Mutal and Lakamha, the cities raised when the last cycle turned, are built up again, and the Maya stand at the threshold of a civilizational renaissance, absorbing the knowledge of every people they have encountered and forging it into something greater.

conditions.text: We own Mutal and its development is at least 3
We own Lakamha and its development is at least 13
Gold at least 3000
Prestige at least 75

event.title: Dawn of the New B'ak'tun
event.text: The daykeepers have announced it: the Long Count calendar has turned to a new B'ak'tun, a great cycle of approximately 394 years. The last time this occurred, the Classic Maya civilization was at its zenith, building Tikal and Palenque. Now the Maya stand once again as a great power, their knowledge encompassing the wisdom of every Mesoamerican civilization. The priests debate the meaning of this new cycle. Some see it as a time of harmony, when the diverse peoples of our realm will become one. Others see it as a time of renewal, when we must rebuild and expand the physical foundations of our civilization.

options.text: This is the age of harmony among peoples.

modifiers.name: B'ak'tun of Harmony
modifiers.text: The new great cycle brings readiness and unity to the Maya people, sharpening their battlefield initiative and recruitment, though the spirit of harmony makes wars of aggression harder to justify.

options.text: This is the age of building and renewal.

modifiers.name: B'ak'tun of Renewal
modifiers.text: The new great cycle is given to rebuilding. Storehouses are filled for the armies and the cities make room for more people, though in the comfort of renewal the word of the throne carries less weight.

destiny.name: The Holcan March
destiny.text: The reach of the Halach Uinic's armies is extended into Honduras and El Salvador. Road stations are raised along the sacbe so that the Holcan can march, and the southern trade routes are brought under Maya military control.

conditions.text: Chose Confederation of the Halach Uinic
Own Naco, or a subject owns it
Own Kuskatan, or a subject owns it
A Sacbe Road Station stands in at least 4 of our locations

event.title: The March of the Holcan
event.text: The Holcan warriors have carried the banner of the Halach Uinic beyond the traditional Maya heartland. Honduras and El Salvador (lands where Maya traders once traveled at the sufferance of local rulers) now answer to the confederation. The great trade hub of Naco, where cacao, obsidian, and jade changed hands between Maya, Lenca, and Pipil merchants, is now firmly under our control. The southern approaches to the Maya world are secure.

options.text: The Holcan have proven their worth.

destiny.name: The Jade Throne
destiny.text: The Holcan are marched into the Valley of Mexico. Azcapotzalco, the seat of the Tepanecs, and Tenochtitlan itself are taken, and the greatest cities on the lake are claimed by the Maya as their own.

conditions.text: Own Tenōchtitlan, or a subject owns it
Own Azcapotzalco, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 50

event.title: The Fall of Tenochtitlan to the Maya
event.text: The unthinkable has been achieved. The Holcan have marched into the Valley of Mexico and taken Tenochtitlan: the greatest city in the Americas, built on an island in a lake, connected by causeways to the mainland, home to markets that dazzle the imagination. The Jade Throne of the Halach Uinic now commands tribute from the former heart of the Aztec world. How shall we govern this vast new domain? We can demand systematic tribute from the conquered peoples, extracting wealth through administration rather than terror. Or we can rule through fear, ensuring that no subject dares contemplate rebellion.

options.text: Extract tribute through administration.

modifiers.name: Jade Throne Tribute
modifiers.text: The conquered peoples of central Mexico render systematic tribute to the Jade Throne, maintained by strong garrisons and a disciplined army that recovers quickly from setbacks.

options.text: Rule through the fear of the Holcan.

modifiers.name: Terror of the Holcan
modifiers.text: The fearsome reputation of the Holcan ensures obedience through devastating assaults, the taking of captives and levies hardened by their example, though peoples who obey out of fear bear the throne no love.

destiny.name: The Fourth Creation
destiny.text: The Popol Vuh speaks of three failed creations before the gods fashioned humanity from corn. Now a Fourth Creation is forged: an empire spanning from Cuba to the Tarascan highlands, held from walled cities.

conditions.text: Own Habana, or a subject owns it
Own Tzintzuntzan, or a subject owns it
A Maya Defensive Wall stands in at least 4 of our locations
Gold at least 3000
Prestige at least 75

event.title: The Fourth Creation
event.text: The Popol Vuh tells that the gods made three failed attempts at creating humanity before succeeding with maize. Now the Maya have completed their own act of creation: an empire that stretches from the Caribbean islands to the Tarascan highlands, from the Gulf coast to the Pacific slopes. This is the Fourth Creation, a new world shaped by Maya hands. The Halach Uinic sits upon the Jade Throne of Tenochtitlan, receiving tribute from a hundred peoples. Shall this empire be maintained through tactical superiority and professional arms, ensuring that our forces can crush any rebellion? Or shall we focus on the political machinery of dominion, building the administrative and diplomatic tools to hold what we have won?

options.text: Our warriors shall maintain the peace.

modifiers.name: Warriors of the Fourth Sun
modifiers.text: The professional army of the Fourth Creation refills its ranks quickly and hires mercenaries cheaply, though the vast military establishment demands a larger government.

options.text: Our administrators shall bind the empire.

modifiers.name: Dominion of the Fourth Creation
modifiers.text: The Maya fleet projects power across the Caribbean while building a naval tradition, though the empire's religious diversity makes holy wars more difficult to wage.

units.name: Holcan Warriors
units.text: Professional Maya warriors armed with obsidian-tipped spears and protected by salt-hardened cotton armor. Masters of jungle ambush and close-quarters combat.

units.name: Obsidian Macemen
units.text: Shock infantry wielding the macuahuitl, a fearsome wooden sword studded with obsidian blades capable of decapitating a horse. They strike hard but wear light armor.

units.name: K'iche' Eagles
units.text: Elite warriors of the K'iche' military tradition, known for rapid flanking movements through difficult terrain and lightning raids on enemy positions.

units.name: Maya War Canoe
units.text: Great dugout canoes capable of carrying forty warriors and their supplies. Fast and maneuverable in coastal waters, they dominate the trade routes of the Caribbean coast.

units.name: Holcan Veterans
units.text: Seasoned Holcan warriors who have survived multiple campaigns. Their experience in jungle warfare, siege defense, and coordinated night raids makes them formidable.

units.name: Atlatl Skirmishers
units.text: Light skirmishers armed with the atlatl spear-thrower, capable of hurling darts with lethal accuracy from concealment in dense jungle undergrowth.

buildings.name: Sacbe Road Station
buildings.text: A waystation along the raised limestone sacbe causeways that connect Maya cities, facilitating trade and communication even during the rainy season.

buildings.name: Maya Observatory
buildings.text: A stone tower with narrow windows aligned to the extreme positions of Venus on the horizon, used by Maya astronomers to calibrate the sacred calendar.

buildings.name: Cacao House
buildings.text: Fermenting and drying sheds among the cacao groves, where the beans are fermented under leaves, dried on mats and roasted for the bitter chocolate prized throughout Mesoamerica as drink, currency and ritual offering. The house raises the cacao harvest of the land.

where.text: The location's raw material is Cocoa

buildings.name: Temple-Pyramid
buildings.text: A massive stepped pyramid crowned by a temple sanctuary, aligned with astronomical events and serving as the religious and political heart of the Maya city.

buildings.name: Obsidian Workshop
buildings.text: A workshop where skilled knappers shape imported volcanic obsidian into razor-edged blades, arrowheads, and the teeth of the macuahuitl war sword.

buildings.name: Cenote Shrine
buildings.text: A sacred shrine built beside a cenote, a natural sinkhole exposing the underground water table, where offerings are made to the rain god Chaak and ancestors.

buildings.name: Maya Ballcourt
buildings.text: A stone court for the sacred ballgame, where teams compete in a ritual contest symbolizing the Hero Twins' victory over the lords of Xibalba. Political alliances and disputes are settled through sacred sport.

buildings.name: Coastal Trading Post
buildings.text: A port facility where great canoes are loaded with cacao, salt, obsidian, and cotton for trade along the Caribbean and Pacific coasts of Mesoamerica.

buildings.name: Maya Defensive Wall
buildings.text: Stone walls and earthworks encircling the acropolis, reinforced with towers and gateways to protect the ruling elite and temple complex from siege.

buildings.name: Salt Works
buildings.text: Shallow pans and boiling sheds on the salt beds of the northern coast, where seawater is dried in the sun or boiled down for a commodity essential to food preservation throughout Mesoamerica. The salt harvest of the land grows with them.

where.text: The location's raw material is Salt

buildings.name: Milpa Terrace
buildings.text: Terraced hillside plots using the ancient milpa intercropping system of maize, beans, and squash, supplemented by modern irrigation techniques.

where.text: Maize is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Forest Palisade
buildings.text: A concealed defensive perimeter of sharpened stakes and ditches hidden within the jungle, designed to channel and slow invading armies into prepared kill zones.

buildings.name: Scribes' Archive
buildings.text: A library and school where Maya scribes are trained in hieroglyphic writing and where bark-paper codices recording astronomy, history, and ritual are preserved.

buildings.name: Astronomical Academy
buildings.text: A grand institution where Maya astronomers, mathematicians, and calendar-keepers synthesize the astronomical knowledge of all Mesoamerican civilizations into a unified system of celestial prediction.

buildings.name: Jaguar War Lodge
buildings.text: An elite military academy where the finest Holcan warriors are trained in siege warfare, combined arms tactics, and the command of multi-ethnic armies drawn from across the empire.

list.name: Halach Uinik
list.text: The Halach Uinik (the True Man) holds judicial, military, and ritual authority over the Cuchcabal of Batab town-headmen. Diego de Landa's Relacion (1566) records the Halach Uinik appointing Batabs to subordinate towns and adjudicating disputes between them. The office is hereditary in a noble lineage; the Cocom of Mayapan traced it to Hunac Ceel. Centralizing the Cuchcabal under one Halach Uinik concentrates loyalty at the cost of the towns' autonomy, and a weak Halach Uinik invites the Batab to feud.

list.name: Holpop Council
list.text: The Holpop ('head of the mat') convenes the popolna council-house where Batabs and elder advisors deliberate. The Holpop holds the woven mat of office, the popol, and the council balances the Halach Uinik's authority through customary right of consultation. K'iche' Q'umarkaj preserved the same institution as the council of the four hereditary lineages (the Kaweq, Nijaib', Sakik, and Tamub') whose deliberations the Popol Vuh records. A working Holpop produces durable legislation; its decay produces faction.

list.name: Ah Kin Priesthood
list.text: The Ah Kin ('he of the sun') form the hierarchical priesthood of the Maya polities. Under the Ah Kin Mai of Mayapan, the priesthood encompasses the Chilam oracular diviners (whose prophecies fill the Chilam Balam books of Chumayel and Tizimin), the Nakom sacrificers, the Chac rain-priests, and the Ah K'in K'ax forest-priests of the wild groves. They keep the 260-day Tzolkin and 365-day Haab counts, select planting dates, and preside over the New Fire ceremonies of every Calendar Round.

list.name: Kaxan'al Codex Network
list.text: The Ah Tz'ib ('he of writing') are the literate scribal class, working with bark-paper screen-fold codices. Four pre-Conquest codices survive (Dresden, Madrid, Paris, and the Maya Codex of Mexico, formerly the Grolier); Diego de Landa burned the rest at the Mani auto-da-fe in 1562. The codices record astronomical tables, divinatory almanacs, ritual schedules, and dynastic histories. The scribal network is tied to the Ah Kin priesthood but distinct: a mathematical-archival profession with its own lineage workshops, providing the throne with literate administrators.

conditions.text: Has embraced Meritocracy

list.name: League of Mayapan
list.text: From around 1200 to 1441 the city of Mayapan housed the joint council of the Cuchcabales: the Cocom (the ruling lineage), the Tutul-Xiu driven from Uxmal, the Itza driven from Chichen, the Cupul, the Chel, the Pech, the Ah Canul, and the Tutul-Xiu of Mani. The Halach Uinik of each house was required to reside at Mayapan, in a system the Spanish observers compared to a hostage league. The Xiu revolt of 1441 ended the league; reviving it re-binds the noble houses to the capital but rule must proceed by consensus of peers.

conditions.text: Owns Màayapáan

list.name: Itza Tribute Flotilla
list.text: The Itza of Tayasal at Noj Petén on Lake Petén Itzá governed a lacustrine and riverine tribute network that outlasted every other Maya polity, falling only in 1697 to Martin de Ursua. The flotilla of trading-canoes plied the Pasion-Usumacinta system and the central Peten lakes, collecting cacao, salt, jade, obsidian, and feathers from subordinate towns. The Kowoj of the eastern lakes operated a parallel system. The flotilla is dual-purpose: the same canoes that gather tribute in peace gather warriors at need.
